claim: YFP-PAD is engineered using the human macrodomain H2A1.1 fused to YFP
source: To visualise whether PARylation events take place during amino-acid starvation, we engineered a PARylation detection probe (PAD) using the human macrodomain H2A1.1 that specifically recognises poly-ADP-ribose (Kustatscher et al., 2005; Timinszky et al., 2009; Forst et al., 2013) fused to YFP (YFP-PAD) (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by Figure 1A showing the probe design. It is also supported by citations to prior work on H2A1.1 macrodomain specificity.

claim: YFP-PAD is both cytoplasmic and nuclear when expressed in Drosophila S2 cells
source: When expressed in Drosophila S2 cells, YFP-PAD is both cytoplasmic and nuclear (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Amino-acid starvation elicits only weak remodelling of YFP-PAD in the cytoplasm and an increase of its nuclear pool
source: Amino-acid starvation only elicits a weak remodelling of the probe in the cytoplasm and an increase of its nuclear pool (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by fluorescence microscopy data comparing growing and starved cells in Figure 1B.

claim: Arsenate treatment of S2 cells elicits YFP-PAD formation into defined cytoplasmic structures
source: Accordingly, YFP-PAD forms defined cytoplasmic structures in arsenate treated S2 cells (Figure 1C) that partially co-localise with stress granules (marked by FMR1, Figure 1C), showing that YFP-PAD is functional.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by fluorescence microscopy data in Figure 1C showing YFP-PAD structures.

claim: YFP-PAD structures formed upon arsenate treatment partially co-localise with stress granules marked by FMR1
source: Accordingly, YFP-PAD forms defined cytoplasmic structures in arsenate treated S2 cells (Figure 1C) that partially co-localise with stress granules (marked by FMR1, Figure 1C), showing that YFP-PAD is functional.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by co-localization data in Figure 1C.

claim: Amino-acid starvation does not elicit detectable PARylation events
source: Taken together, these results indicate that amino-acid starvation does not elicit detectable PARylation events.
evidence: The claim is directly stated as a conclusion from the YFP-PAD experiments showing minimal remodeling during amino-acid starvation.

claim: GFP-MAD is engineered based upon macrodomains 1-3 of human PARP14
source: Therefore, the PARP14 macrodomains 1–3 were GFP-tagged at their N-terminus, and a linker was inserted to preserve their binding capabilities (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by Figure 2A showing the probe design.

claim: PARP14 macrodomains 1-3 bind specifically MARylated, but not PARylated, substrates in vitro
source: Last, hPARP14 macrodomains 1–3 bind specifically MARylated, but not PARylated, substrates in vitro (Forst et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Forst et al., 2013.

claim: GFP-MAD is diffuse in the cytoplasm and absent from the nucleus in most transfected S2 cells under growing conditions
source: When expressed in S2 cells under growing conditions, GFP-MAD is diffuse in the cytoplasm in most of the transfected cells, but in contrast to YFP-PAD is absent from the nucleus (Figure 2B,B').
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by fluorescence microscopy data in Figure 2B,B'.

claim: GFP-MAD forms spots in S2 cells upon amino-acid starvation in a time-dependent manner
source: When cells are starved of amino-acids for increasing length of time, GFP-MAD adopts a defined pattern. After 1 hr, it concentrates in one spot in a low percentage of cells (arrows in Figure 2B,B'). After 2 hr, it forms 1–3 spots in a larger number of cells. Thereafter, the number of spots (some of them with a U/donut shape) (arrowheads, Figure 2B–E) increases and they tend to concentrate in the middle of the cell after 4 hr (not shown).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by time-course fluorescence microscopy data in Figure 2B,B'.

claim: The G1055E mutation in GFP-MAD completely abrogates its binding to mono-ADP-ribose in vitro
source: This mutation affects the ADP-ribose binding pocket and therefore interferes with the ADP-binding activity (Forst et al., 2013) and in vitro to completely abrogate its binding to mono-ADP-ribose (Dani et al., 2009; Karras et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citations to Dani et al., 2009 and Karras et al., 2005.

claim: G1055E GFP-MAD does not form spots upon amino-acid starvation and remains diffuse in the cytoplasm
source: Strikingly, amino-acid starvation of S2 cells expressing G1055E GFP-MAD does not result in any pattern and the mutant probe remains diffuse in the cytoplasm (Figure 2C,C').
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by fluorescence microscopy data in Figure 2C,C'.

claim: GFP-MAD spots start forming about 1 hr after amino-acid starvation and accumulate
source: Next, we visualised MARylation events in live cells. This confirms that MAD spots start forming about 1 hr after starvation and accumulate.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by live cell imaging data referenced in Figure 2D and Video 1.

claim: GFP-MAD spots are overall stable with an average lifetime of 50 min for some transient spots
source: It also shows that they are overall stable, (Figure 2D and Video 1), although few appear more transient with an average lifetime of 50 min (not shown).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by live cell imaging data in Figure 2D and Video 1.

claim: GFP-MAD spots correspond to non-membrane bound structures ranging from 600 nm to two microns in diameter
source: Using a Fluorescence-to-ImmunoEM correlative method (Vicidomini et al., 2010; Hassink et al., 2012), we showed that GFP-MAD spots correspond to non-membrane bound structures (Figure 2E,E'), ranging from 600 nm to two microns in diameter.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by correlative fluorescence/IEM data in Figure 2E,E' and citations to the methods.

claim: GFP-MAD spots are fully reversible after 30 min of Schneider's medium addition following starvation
source: We tested their reversibility upon nutrient replenishment following starvation and found that they are fully reversible after 30 min of Schneider's addition (Figure 2F,F').
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by fluorescence microscopy data in Figure 2F,F'.

claim: Heat stress does not elicit a GFP-MAD pattern
source: Last, we show that heat stress (Figure 2G,G') and arsenate treatment (not shown) do not elicit a GFP-MAD pattern, confirming the specificity of MARylation to amino-acid starvation.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by fluorescence microscopy data in Figure 2G,G'.

claim: Arsenate treatment does not elicit a GFP-MAD pattern
source: Last, we show that heat stress (Figure 2G,G') and arsenate treatment (not shown) do not elicit a GFP-MAD pattern, confirming the specificity of MARylation to amino-acid starvation.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text.

claim: Three additional Drosophila PARPs were identified: CG4719 (homologous to human Tankyrase), CG15925 (homologous to human PARP16), and CG18812 (homologous to human GDAP2)
source: In line with (Hottiger et al., 2010), we identified three additional ORFs: CG4719 is homologous to human Tankyrase, CG15925 is homologous to human PARP16, and CG18812 is homologous to human GDAP2, a macrodomain, not a PARP (Rack et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citations to Hottiger et al., 2010 and Rack et al., 2016.

claim: dPARP16 depletion completely prevents GFP-MAD spot formation upon amino-acid starvation
source: First, dPARP16 depletion completely prevents their formation upon amino-acid starvation and GFP-MAD remains diffuse in the cytoplasm (Figure 3A,A').
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by fluorescence microscopy data in Figure 3A,A'.

claim: Depletion of dPARP1 and dTNK has no effect on GFP-MAD spot formation
source: In comparison, the depletion of the other PARPs has no effect and GFP-MAD spots form as in mock-depleted cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by fluorescence microscopy data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Overexpression of dPARP16 under growing conditions induces robust formation of GFP-MAD spots in most cells
source: Second, the overexpression of dPARP16 under growing conditions induces the robust formation of GFP-MAD spots in most of the cells (Figure 3B,B',E).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by fluorescence microscopy data in Figure 3B,B',E.

claim: 84 ± 6% of GFP-MAD spots formed upon dPARP16 overexpression partially or completely co-localize with the enzyme
source: Importantly, 84 ± 6% of GFP-MAD spots formed upon dPARP16 overexpression partially or completely co-localize with the enzyme (Figure 3B,B').
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by co-localization data in Figure 3B,B'.

claim: dPARP16 is the closest homolog of human PARP16
source: dPARP16 is the closest homolog of human PARP16 as shown by building a phylogenetic tree containing dPARP16 and all human PARPs (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by phylogenetic analysis in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The catalytic site of dPARP16 consists of the YYY triad (Y199, Y221, Y284)
source: Human PARP16 has a catalytic site comprising the triad HYY (Hottiger et al., 2010) and using HHpred, we predicted that the catalytic site of dPARP16 consists of the YYY triad (Y199, Y221, Y284) (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by sequence analysis in Figure 3—figure supplement 3 and citation to Hottiger et al., 2010.

claim: dPARP16 is predicted to be membrane anchored with catalytic domain facing the cytoplasm
source: Last, as hPARP16, dPARP16 is also predicted to be membrane anchored with catalytic domain facing the cytoplasm (Jwa and Chang, 2012; Di Paola et al., 2012) (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by structural prediction in Figure 3C and citations to Jwa and Chang, 2012 and Di Paola et al., 2012.

claim: dPARP16 localises to the ER
source: Accordingly, we find that dPARP16 localises to ER (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by immunofluorescence and IEM data in Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: Expression of dPARP16 Y221A catalytic mutant does not lead to the formation of GFP-MAD spots
source: We showed that its expression does not lead to the formation of GFP-MAD spot (Figure 3D,F), whereas expression of the wild type dPARP16 does (Figure 3B,B',F).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by fluorescence microscopy data in Figure 3D,F.

claim: Expression of ΔTM dPARP16 does not induce the formation of GFP-MAD spots
source: Unlike the wild type protein (Figure 3B',F), expression of the ΔTM dPARP16 does not induce the formation of GFP-MAD spots (arrowheads in Figure 3E,F), indicating that dPARP16 membrane anchoring is required for its MARylation activity.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by fluorescence microscopy data in Figure 3E,F.

claim: Expression of dPARP16 does not elicit a PARylation pattern using YFP-PAD
source: Last, we show expression of dPARP16 does not elicit a PARylation pattern using YFP-PAD (Figure 3G,G').
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by fluorescence microscopy data in Figure 3G,G'.

claim: Sec bodies are pro-survival cytoplasmic stress assemblies that form upon amino-acid starvation in Drosophila cells
source: Sec body formation results from the inhibition of a major anabolic pathway, the protein transport through the secretory pathway, upon amino-acid starvation of Drosophila cells (Amodio et al., 2009; Zacharogianni et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citations to Amodio et al., 2009 and Zacharogianni et al., 2014.

claim: Sec bodies appear as bright circular structures of 700 ± 100 nm in diameter by immunofluorescence
source: By immunofluorescence, Sec bodies appear as bright circular structures of 700 ± 100 nm in diameter (confirmed by immuno-electron microscopy, IEM) and there are typically 7 ± 3 Sec bodies per starved cell (Zacharogianni et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Zacharogianni et al., 2014.

claim: dPARP16 depletion completely prevents Sec body formation upon amino-acid starvation
source: We found that dPARP16 depletion completely prevents Sec body formation upon amino-acid starvation (Figure 4B,B').
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 4B,B'.

claim: dPARP16 depletion strongly affects cell survival upon amino-acid starvation and cell recovery upon stress relief
source: In agreement with this, dPARP16 depletion also strongly affects cell survival upon amino-acid starvation as well as cell recovery upon stress relief (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by cell viability data in Figure 4C.

claim: In dPARP16 depleted cells during growing conditions cell survival is unaffected
source: In contrast, in dPARP16 depleted cells during growing conditions cell survival is unaffected, indicating that dPARP16 plays a crucial role exclusively upon starvation.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by cell viability data referenced in Figure 4C.

claim: Expression of dPARP16 quantitatively drives the specific formation of Sec bodies under growing conditions
source: Furthermore, expression of dPARP16 quantitatively drives the specific formation of Sec bodies under growing conditions (Figure 4D, arrows, Figure 4D').
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 4D,D'.

claim: Depletion of dPARP1 and dTNK does not affect Sec body formation
source: Accordingly, depletion (Figure 4—figure supplement 1) and overexpression (Figure 4—figure supplement 2) of dPARP1 and dTNK do not affect Sec body formation.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1 and 2.

claim: Expression of dPARP16 catalytic mutants (Y199A and Y221A) does not lead to Sec body formation
source: Whereas expression of wild type PARP16 leads to Sec body formation, the expression of dPARP16 catalytic mutants (Y199A and Y221A) do not (Figure 5A,A').
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 5A,A'.

claim: Expression of Y199A dPARP16 does not rescue Sec body formation in starved dPARP16 depleted cells
source: To confirm this result, we show that the expression of Y199A dPARP16 does not rescue Sec body formation in starved dPARP16 depleted cells, whereas the expression of wild type dPARP16 does (Figure 5B,B').
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 5B,B'.

claim: Expression of ΔTM dPARP16 does not induce Sec body formation
source: We show that unlike the wild type protein, it does not induce Sec body formation (Figure 5C,A', arrowheads).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 5C,A'.

claim: dPARP16 localises near or around Sec bodies
source: In support of this, we found that dPARP16 localises near or around Sec bodies (Figure 5C,D, small green arrows), suggesting that Sec body components could be dPARP16 MARylated substrates.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 5C,D.

claim: A large proportion of GFP-MAD spots that form after 1-2 hr incubation in KRB overlap with, or are in close proximity to, ERES and small forming Sec bodies
source: We found that a large proportion of GFP-MAD spots that form after 1-2 hr incubation in KRB overlap with, or are in close proximity to, ERES and small forming Sec bodies (Figure 6A,A'), suggesting that ERES components could be MARylated prior to Sec body formation.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by co-localization data in Figure 6A,A'.

claim: Up to 40% of Sec bodies after 3 hr incubation in KRB are formed adjacent to, or overlapping with, GFP-MAD spots
source: Furthermore, we found that a significant number of Sec bodies (up to 40% after 3 hr incubation in KRB) are formed adjacent to, or overlapping with, GFP-MAD spots (Figure 6B,B', arrowheads).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by co-localization data in Figure 6B,B'.

claim: A small but consistent pool of Sec16 is observed within the GFP-MAD spots
source: In agreement, a small but consistent pool of Sec16 is observed within the GFP-MAD spots (Figure 6C,D).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by IEM data in Figure 6C,D.

claim: Cherry-MAD strongly co-localises with Sec16-GFP-CAAX at the plasma membrane upon amino-acid starvation
source: However, it strongly co-localises with Sec16-GFP-CAAX at the plasma membrane upon amino-acid starvation (Figure 7A',E).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by fluorescence microscopy data in Figure 7A',E.

claim: Cherry-MAD is not recruited to the plasma membrane by Sec23-GFP-CAAX upon amino-acid starvation
source: Interestingly, cherry-MAD is not recruited to the plasma membrane by Sec23-GFP-CAAX (Figure 7B,E) upon amino-acid starvation, suggesting substrate specificity.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by fluorescence microscopy data in Figure 7B,E.

claim: GFP-MAD binds Sec16 significantly more upon amino-acid starvation than under growing conditions
source: GFP-MAD binds Sec16 significantly more upon amino-acid starvation than under growing conditions and more than GFP (Figure 7C,D).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by immunoprecipitation data in Figure 7C,D.

claim: Sec23, FMR1, Caprin and Rasputin are not pulled down by GFP-MAD upon amino-acid starvation
source: To further test the specificity of the GFP-MAD/Sec16 interaction, we investigated whether Sec23 (Figure 7D) and RNA binding proteins (FMR1, Caprin and Rasputin) (Figure 7C and not shown) are also pulled down by GFP-MAD upon amino-acid starvation. We found that neither of them are.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by immunoprecipitation data in Figure 7C,D.

claim: Truncation of Sec16 C-terminus (ΔCter-GFP-CAAX) completely abolishes cherry-MAD recruitment to the plasma membrane upon starvation
source: In contrast, truncation of Sec16 C-terminus (ΔCter-GFP-CAAX) completely abolishes cherry-MAD recruitment to the plasma membrane upon starvation (Figure 7E).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by fluorescence microscopy data in Figure 7E.

claim: Co-expression of Cter-GFP-CAAX with cherry-MAD results in the strong recruitment of cherry-MAD to the plasma membrane
source: Accordingly, co-expression of Cter-GFP-CAAX with cherry-MAD results in the strong recruitment of cherry-MAD to the plasma membrane (Figure 7E; Figure 7—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by fluorescence microscopy data in Figure 7E and Figure 7—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Expression of SRDC-GFP-CAAX leads to the robust recruitment of cherry-MAD to the plasma membrane upon amino-acid starvation
source: Strikingly, expression of SRDC-GFP-CAAX leads to the robust recruitment of cherry-MAD to the plasma membrane upon amino-acid starvation (Figure 7E; Figure 7—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by fluorescence microscopy data in Figure 7E and Figure 7—figure supplement 2D.

claim: Sec16 lacking SRDC (ΔSRDC-GFP-CAAX) is unable to recruit cherry-MAD to the plasma membrane
source: In agreement, Sec16 lacking SRDC (ΔSRDC-GFP-CAAX) in Sec16 depleted cells (to prevent oligomerisation with endogenous Sec16) is unable to recruit cherry-MAD to the plasma membrane (Figure 7E; Figure 7—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by fluorescence microscopy data in Figure 7E and Figure 7—figure supplement 2E.

claim: Expression of SRDC-GFP results in the efficient formation of Sec bodies in the absence of stress
source: Strikingly, this results in the efficient formation of the Sec bodies in the absence of stress (Figure 8A,D), a phenotype strongly reminiscent of dPARP16 overexpression (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 8A,D.

claim: dPARP16 is critically necessary for SRDC-induced Sec body formation
source: Accordingly, we found that dPARP16 is critically necessary for SRDC-induced Sec body formation, since they were not formed in dPARP16 depleted cells (Figure 8B,D).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 8B,D.

claim: SRD-GFP expression does not induce Sec body formation
source: Importantly, SRD-GFP expression does not induced Sec body formation (Figure 8C,D).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 8C,D.

claim: Transfection of Sec16-GFP and SRDC-GFP significantly rescues Sec body formation in Sec16 depleted cells
source: As expected, Sec16 depleted cells do not form Sec bodies (here marked by Sec23) upon amino-acid starvation (Figure 8H), and transfection of Sec16-GFP (Figure 8E,H) and SRDC-GFP (Figure 8F,H) significantly rescues this formation.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 8E,F,H.

claim: Transfection of ΔSRDC-GFP does not rescue Sec body formation in Sec16 depleted cells
source: However, transfection of ΔSRDC-GFP does not, demonstrating the direct role of SRDC in Sec body formation.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by immunofluorescence data referenced in Figure 8G,H.

claim: The macrodomains of human PARP14 are more efficient at detecting MARylation in S2 cells than those from mouse PARP14
source: Note that the macrodomains of human PARP14 are more efficient at detecting MARylation in S2 cells than those from mouse PARP14 that were originally used by (Forst et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is stated in the legend of Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and supported by comparison data in the figure.

claim: The insertion of a linker greatly improved the GFP-MAD probe sensitivity and/or efficiency
source: Furthermore, the insertion of a linker greatly improved the probe sensitivity and/or efficiency.
evidence: The claim is stated in the legend of Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and supported by comparison data in the figure.

claim: Overexpression of dPARP16 leads to a strong re-arrangement of the ER marked by calnexin
source: Overexpression of dPARP16 leads to a strong re-arrangement of the ER marked by calnexin (A) that appears to accumulate at the nuclear envelop (arrows) and KDEL receptor that appears to concentrate near the cell cortex (B, arrowheads).
evidence: The claim is stated in the legend of Figure 3—figure supplement 5 and supported by immunofluorescence data in the figure.

claim: The same ER re-arrangements observed upon dPARP16 overexpression are observed upon amino-acid starvation
source: Interestingly, the same ER re-arrangements are observed upon amino-acid starvation for both markers (A' and B').
evidence: The claim is stated in the legend of Figure 3—figure supplement 5 and supported by immunofluorescence data in the figure.

claim: PARP catalysed ADP-ribosylation is a post-translational modification involved in several physiological and pathological processes, including cellular stress
source: PARP catalysed ADP-ribosylation is a post-translational modification involved in several physiological and pathological processes, including cellular stress.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the abstract.

claim: Amino-acid starvation triggers an unprecedented display of mono-ADP-ribosylation
source: Using them, we show that amino-acid starvation triggers an unprecedented display of mono-ADP-ribosylation that governs the formation of Sec body, a recently identified stress assembly that forms in Drosophila cells.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: dPARP16 catalytic activity is necessary and sufficient for both amino-acid starvation induced mono-ADP-ribosylation and subsequent Sec body formation and cell survival
source: We show that dPARP16 catalytic activity is necessary and sufficient for both amino-acid starvation induced mono-ADP-ribosylation and subsequent Sec body formation and cell survival.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: dPARP16 catalyses the modification of Sec16, a key Sec body component
source: Importantly, dPARP16 catalyses the modification of Sec16, a key Sec body component, and we show that it is a critical event for the formation of this stress assembly.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: PARPs are a family of 17 proteins in mammals
source: It is catalysed by PARPs (also called ADP-Ribose Transferase class D, ARTD), a family of 17 proteins in mammals (Hottiger et al., 2010; Leung et al., 2011; Leung, 2014).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citations to Hottiger et al., 2010; Leung et al., 2011; Leung, 2014.

claim: PARP1 is required for DNA repair during DNA damage
source: The founding member, the nuclear PARP1, is required for DNA repair during DNA damage (Gibson and Kraus, 2012) where it hyper-PARylates itself as well as surrounding histones (Gibbs-Seymour et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citations to Gibson and Kraus, 2012 and Gibbs-Seymour et al., 2016.

claim: MARylation is linked to ER stress via PARP16
source: Furthermore, MARylation is linked to ER stress via PARP16, the only membrane-anchored member of this family (Jwa and Chang, 2012; Di Paola et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citations to Jwa and Chang, 2012 and Di Paola et al., 2012.

claim: Most PARPs are predicted to be MARylation enzymes
source: However, these antibodies bind poly-, not mono-ADP-ribose. This represents a serious limitation as most PARPs are predicted to be MARylation enzymes (Hottiger et al., 2010; Leung, 2014; Bütepage et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citations to Hottiger et al., 2010; Leung, 2014; Bütepage et al., 2015.

claim: Macrodomains H2A1.1 show binding specificity for PARylated proteins
source: Accordingly, macrodomains H2A1.1 show binding specificity for PARylated proteins (Kustatscher et al., 2005; Timinszky et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citations to Kustatscher et al., 2005 and Timinszky et al., 2009.

claim: Macrodomains from human PARP14 exclusively bind Mono-ADP-ribose
source: And macrodomains from human PARP14 that exclusively binds Mono-ADP-ribose have being used to pull down MARylated PARP10 (Forst et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Forst et al., 2013.

claim: PARP14 macrodomains do not exhibit hydrolase activity
source: Importantly these macrodomains do not exhibit hydrolase activity (Rosenthal et al., 2013; Jankevicius et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citations to Rosenthal et al., 2013 and Jankevicius et al., 2013.

claim: Sec body formation results from the inhibition of protein transport through the secretory pathway upon amino-acid starvation
source: Sec body formation results from the inhibition of a major anabolic pathway, the protein transport through the secretory pathway, upon amino-acid starvation of Drosophila cells (Amodio et al., 2009; Zacharogianni et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citations to Amodio et al., 2009 and Zacharogianni et al., 2014.

claim: COPII formation requires Sar1, its GEF Sec12 and the structural proteins forming the coat itself, Sec23/24 and Sec13/31
source: COPII formation requires Sar1, its GEF Sec12 and the structural proteins forming the coat itself, Sec23/24 and Sec13/31 (Miller and Schekman, 2013) as well as the large hydrophilic scaffold protein Sec16 (Sprangers and Rabouille, 2015).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citations to Miller and Schekman, 2013 and Sprangers and Rabouille, 2015.

claim: Sec bodies have liquid droplet properties
source: The inhibition of protein transport through the secretory pathway upon amino-acid starvation is accompanied by the remodeling of ERES and the formation of a novel type of pro-survival stress assembly with liquid droplet properties, the Sec body, where COPII coat proteins and Sec16 are stored and protected from degradation during the period of stress (Zacharogianni et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Zacharogianni et al., 2014.

claim: COPII coat proteins and Sec16 are stored and protected from degradation in Sec bodies during amino-acid starvation
source: The inhibition of protein transport through the secretory pathway upon amino-acid starvation is accompanied by the remodeling of ERES and the formation of a novel type of pro-survival stress assembly with liquid droplet properties, the Sec body, where COPII coat proteins and Sec16 are stored and protected from degradation during the period of stress (Zacharogianni et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Zacharogianni et al., 2014.

claim: Sec16 MARylation on its C-terminus is an amino-acid starvation specific event
source: Last, we identify the ERES component Sec16 as a novel dPARP16 substrate and show that it is MARylated on its C-terminus in an amino-acid starvation specific manner.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Sec16 MARylation initiates the formation of Sec bodies
source: We propose that this event initiates the formation of the Sec bodies and poses Sec16 as a stress response protein.
evidence: The claim is directly stated as a proposal based on the experimental findings.

claim: The macrodomain-based probes are useful and specific tools to follow ADP-ribosylation in vitro and in vivo
source: Furthermore, this demonstrates that the macrodomain-based probes that we built are useful and specific tools to follow ADP-ribosylation taking place during biological processes in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: The claim is directly stated as a conclusion from the experimental findings.

claim: dPARP16 is a novel key factor in cell survival to amino-acid starvation
source: In this regard, we have identified dPARP16 as a novel key factor in cell survival to amino-acid starvation.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by cell viability data.

claim: GFP-MAD specifically detects and binds Mono-ADP-ribose
source: First, MAD specifically detects and binds Mono-ADP-ribose.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Discussion section and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: The affinity of PARP14 macrodomains for mono-ADP-ribose required for in vivo visualisation is provided by the three macrodomains together in a cooperative manner
source: Crystallography and calorimetric assays show that each macrodomain has a conserved fold with high binding affinity for mono-ADP-ribose (particularly macrodomains 2 and 3) and the affinity required for in vivo visualisation is provided by the three macrodomains together in a cooperative manner.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by reference to crystallography and calorimetric assays.

claim: GFP-MAD allows the visualisation of an unprecedented display of MARylation events upon amino-acid starvation under the form of non-membrane bound, reversible spots/rings in the cytoplasm
source: In this regard, GFP-MAD allows the visualisation of an unprecedented display of MARylation events upon amino-acid starvation (but not heat shock or arsenate poisoning) under the form of non-membrane bound, reversible spots/rings in the cytoplasm.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: This is the first time that MARylation response is visualised in real time during stress
source: To the best of our knowledge, this is the first time that MARylation response is visualised in real time during stress.
evidence: The claim is directly stated as a conclusion from the experimental findings.

claim: GFP-MAD spots represent a concentration of MARylated substrates reflecting local dPARP16 activation
source: We propose that GFP-MAD spots represent a concentration of MARylated substrates reflecting local dPARP16 activation.
evidence: The claim is directly stated as a proposal based on the experimental findings.

claim: GFP-MAD is an efficient activity sensor of the nutrient stress response
source: This makes GFP-MAD, an efficient activity sensor of the nutrient stress response and dPARP16 the key MARylation enzyme eliciting this response.
evidence: The claim is directly stated as a conclusion from the experimental findings.

claim: dPARP16 is necessary and sufficient for Sec body formation upon amino-acid starvation
source: dPARP16 is necessary and sufficient for Sec body formation upon amino-acid starvation and this creates an unprecedented link between MARylation, metabolic stress and the formation of stress assembly.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: dPARP16 creates an unprecedented link between MARylation, metabolic stress and the formation of stress assembly
source: dPARP16 is necessary and sufficient for Sec body formation upon amino-acid starvation and this creates an unprecedented link between MARylation, metabolic stress and the formation of stress assembly.
evidence: The claim is directly stated as a conclusion from the experimental findings.

claim: dPARP16 is a key survival factor upon amino-acid starvation
source: This makes dPARP16 a key survival factor upon amino-acid starvation.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by cell viability data.

claim: Nutrient starvation in yeast leads to storage of metabolic enzymes in reversible assemblies
source: Nutrient starvation in yeast also leads to storage of metabolic enzymes in reversible assemblies (Narayanaswamy et al., 2009), such as glutamine synthetase (Petrovska et al., 2014) or proteasome subunits (Peters et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citations to Narayanaswamy et al., 2009; Petrovska et al., 2014; Peters et al., 2013.

claim: Large Sec bodies did not form in mammalian cells upon conditions used for Drosophila cells
source: We have reported that large Sec bodies did not form in mammalian cells upon conditions used for Drosophila cells, although a remodelling of the early secretory pathway was observed (Zacharogianni et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Zacharogianni et al., 2014.

claim: dPARP16 has a very low transcriptional level when compared to most genes according to RNAseq data
source: According to our RNAseq data of S2 cells in growing conditions and upon amino-acid starvation conditions (unpublished), dPARP16 has a very low transcriptional level when compared to most genes, suggesting that its protein level is also low.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by unpublished RNAseq data.

claim: dPARP16 overexpression leads to its activation
source: Because dPARP16 moderate overexpression in growing cells leads the detection of MARylation events, it suggests that dPARP16 overexpression leads to its activation.
evidence: The claim is directly stated as an inference from the experimental findings.

claim: dPARP16 level needs to be kept low in basal conditions to avoid its activation
source: This also suggests that dPARP16 level needs to be kept low in basal conditions to avoid its activation, challenging the detection of its activity in basal conditions.
evidence: The claim is directly stated as an inference from the experimental findings.

claim: TORC1 activation is not involved in Sec body formation
source: Given the nature of the stress, TORC1 activation would be an ideal pathway but we have shown that it is not involved in Sec body formation (Zacharogianni et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Zacharogianni et al., 2014.

claim: In mammalian cells, PARP16 is activated via auto-MARylation triggered by ER stress
source: In mammalian cells, PARP16 is activated via auto-MARylation triggered by ER stress (Jwa and Chang, 2012).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Jwa and Chang, 2012.

claim: Mammalian PARP16 MARylates two key kinases of the ER stress response UPR, Ire1 and PERK, leading to their activation
source: As a result, it MARylates two key kinases of the ER stress response UPR, Ire1 and PERK (Gardner et al., 2013), leading to their activation (Jwa and Chang, 2012) and the unfolded Protein Response.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citations to Gardner et al., 2013 and Jwa and Chang, 2012.

claim: Inducing ER stress does not lead to Sec body formation
source: However, we have previously shown (Zacharogianni et al., 2014) and our unpublished results) that inducing ER stress does not lead to Sec body formation.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Zacharogianni et al., 2014 and unpublished results.

claim: Cell survival is significantly more affected by amino-acid starvation than by ER stress
source: This result is reinforced by the demonstration that cell survival is significantly more affected by amino-acid starvation than by ER stress (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by cell viability data in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: dPARP16 appears to be more critical for amino-acid starvation than for ER stress
source: As a result, dPARP16 appears to be more critical for amino-acid starvation than for ER stress (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by cell viability data in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: Karyopherin is a substrate of mammalian PARP16
source: Another substrate of mammalian PARP16 is karyopherin (Di Paola et al., 2012), a component required for nuclear export.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Di Paola et al., 2012.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of nuclear export does not inhibit Sec body formation
source: However, our unpublished results shows that the pharmacological inhibition of nuclear export does not inhibit Sec body formation (not shown), suggesting that at least during amino-acid starvation, karyopherin might not play a prominent role and that dPARP16 has different substrates.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by unpublished results.

claim: The discovery of SRDC is reminiscent to the existence of an Amyloid Converting Peptide in proteins found in nuclear amyloid bodies in cells upon several stress
source: The discovery of a short peptide required for the formation of Sec bodies is reminiscent to the existence of an Amyloid Converting Peptide in proteins found in nuclear amyloid bodies in cells upon several stress (Audas et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Audas et al., 2016.

claim: Amyloidogenesis is mediated by an Amyloid Converting Peptide motif binding a long non-coding RNA
source: Interestingly, amyloidogenesis is mediated by this motif binding a long non-coding RNA that could be equivalent or comparable to the SRDC MARylation during Sec body formation.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by reference to amyloidogenesis mechanism.

claim: In the context of the full-length endogenous protein, SRDC MARylation could act as both a signalling and structural event allowing the recruitment of Sec16 and other ERES components into Sec bodies
source: In the context of the full-length endogenous protein, SRDC MARylation could act as both a signalling and structural event allowing the recruitment of Sec16 and other ERES components into Sec bodies.
evidence: The claim is directly stated as a speculation based on the experimental findings.

claim: SRDC on its own may act only as a signalling event for Sec body formation
source: However, SRCD on its own is not recruited to Sec bodies, and our interpretation is that it may act only as a signalling event for Sec body formation.
evidence: The claim is directly stated as an interpretation based on the experimental findings.

claim: MARylated Sec16 forms a signalling platform that would lead to the modifications of other Sec body components allowing their incorporation
source: Although this is consistent with the protein packing and competing binding that takes place during the formation of stress assemblies (that most likely would exclude GFP-MAD), it might also suggest that MARylated Sec16 forms a signalling platform. This would lead to the modifications of other Sec body components allowing their incorporation (Figure 8I).
evidence: The claim is directly stated as a speculation based on the experimental findings and supported by the model in Figure 8I.

claim: PARylation has been proposed to preferentially occur on LCSs (Low complexity sequences)
source: Interestingly, PARylation has been proposed to preferentially occur on LCSs (Low complexity sequences, that is, region of poor amino-acid diversity) (Leung, 2014).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Leung, 2014.

claim: Sec16 is rich in LCSs
source: Sec16 is rich in LCSs (Zacharogianni et al., 2014) and SRDC is intrinsically disordered, therefore accessible to be modified by dPARP16.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Zacharogianni et al., 2014.

claim: SRDC is intrinsically disordered
source: Sec16 is rich in LCSs (Zacharogianni et al., 2014) and SRDC is intrinsically disordered, therefore accessible to be modified by dPARP16.
evidence: The claim is directly stated as an inference from the experimental findings.

claim: Sec16 is a stress response protein
source: Taken together, we postulate that Sec16 is a stress response protein and a new substrate for the pro-survival dPARP16 upon amino-acid starvation
evidence: The claim is directly stated as a postulate based on the experimental findings.
